title: axross-mcp-hub
description: Curated, audited, container-packaged MCP servers for authorized security work (reverse engineering, firmware and forensics, network recon, web, OSINT, secrets, password cracking), built by https://github.com/c0decave/axross-mcp-hub and pinned by digest.

entries.name: binwalk
entries.title: binwalk
entries.description: Firmware analysis with binwalk: signature scan, extraction of embedded archives and file systems (SquashFS, CPIO, 7z, zip, gzip, xz, bzip2, LZO), entropy analysis and hex dumps. Files are read from the folder mounted at /work. Extraction writes to a writable folder mounted at /out, else to the container's /tmp (64 MiB, gone when the server stops). No network.

mounts.description: The folder with the firmware images (read-only is enough)
A folder for extracted files (tick writable)

entries.notes: Extraction runs third-party extractors on untrusted input inside the container (no capabilities, no network). Mount /out writable only when you want the extracted files kept.

entries.name: capa
entries.title: capa (Mandiant)
entries.description: Finds the capabilities of a PE, ELF or .NET binary or shellcode with Mandiant capa and the capa-rules set, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and MBC. Files are read from the folder mounted at /work (capa_analyze takes /work/<file>). No network.
entries.license: MIT (MCP server, FuzzingLabs) AND Apache-2.0 (capa, capa-rules)

mounts.description: The folder with the samples to analyze (read-only is enough)

entries.notes: Large binaries can exceed axross's 512 MiB container memory limit or the 300 s default timeout; capa_analyze takes a timeout of up to 3600 s.

entries.name: crtsh
entries.title: crt.sh (Certificate Transparency)
entries.description: Subdomains and certificates of a domain from the Certificate Transparency logs through crt.sh: every logged certificate for a domain and its subdomains with the unique host names they name, and a single certificate as PEM. Needs network: Allowlist with crt.sh:443 (axross's proxy; nothing else is reachable).
entries.notes: Passive: only crt.sh is asked, the domain itself is never contacted. crt.sh is a free service that is sometimes slow or overloaded; the tool then says so.

entries.name: dnstwist
entries.title: dnstwist
entries.description: Finds look-alike domains of a domain (typosquatting, homographs, bitsquatting, TLD swaps, ...) with dnstwist: dnstwist_permutations works offline; dnstwist_scan resolves them (A, AAAA, NS, MX) and needs network: Full (DNS). No web fetching, WHOIS or GeoIP.
entries.notes: Without network dnstwist_permutations still works; dnstwist_scan then reports every domain as unresolved.

entries.name: exiftool
entries.title: ExifTool
entries.description: Reads the metadata of images, videos, audio, PDFs, Office documents and many other formats with ExifTool 13.25 (EXIF, IPTC, XMP, GPS, maker notes, ...), all tags or a chosen subset with wildcards. Files are read from the folder mounted at /work. Read-only: this build offers no writing or removing of metadata. No network.
entries.license: MIT (MCP server, joshmsimpson/exiftool_mcp, patched) AND Artistic-1.0 OR GPL-1.0-or-later (ExifTool, Debian package)

mounts.description: The folder with the files to inspect (read-only is enough)

entries.notes: Patched: requested tag names filter ExifTool's JSON in Python instead of becoming ExifTool options (upstream let a tag such as "if" run Perl code); the write and remove tools are removed.

entries.name: ffuf
entries.title: ffuf
entries.description: Web fuzzing with ffuf 2.1: directory and file discovery, virtual hosts, parameters and custom FUZZ positions, with status, size, word and line filters and bundled SecLists wordlists (common, raft-small-dirs, raft-small-files, subdomains-top1mil, params-top) or your own wordlists from /work. Needs network: Full (requests go to the target you name).
entries.license: MIT (MCP server, FuzzingLabs, patched; ffuf; SecLists)

mounts.description: Optional: a folder with your own wordlists (read-only is enough)

entries.notes: Fuzz only systems you are authorized to test. Every argument is validated; a wordlist is a bundled name or a file under /work, never another container path.

entries.name: floss
entries.title: FLOSS
entries.description: Mandiant FLOSS 3.2: extracts obfuscated strings from malware - static strings plus stack strings, tight strings and strings decoded by emulating the sample's decoding routines (vivisect; the sample is never executed) - from PE files and shellcode, language-aware for Go and Rust. Samples are read from the folder mounted at /work. No network.
entries.license: MIT (MCP server, axross-mcp-hub) AND Apache-2.0 (FLOSS, vivisect)

mounts.description: The folder with the samples (read-only is enough)

entries.notes: Emulation of large samples is slow and memory-hungry; axross's 512 MiB limit applies - use only=["static"] or a smaller timeout for big files.

entries.name: gitleaks
entries.title: gitleaks
entries.description: Finds secrets - API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys - in files and in the whole history of git repositories with gitleaks 8.30 and its built-in rules (or your .toml rules). Findings name rule, file, line, commit, author and date; secrets are redacted in the answer unless asked otherwise. Paths are read from the folder mounted at /work. No network.
entries.license: MIT (MCP server, axross-mcp-hub; gitleaks) AND GPL-2.0 (git, Debian package)

mounts.description: The folder or repository to scan (read-only is enough)

entries.notes: A scanned repository's own git configuration cannot make git run programs: textconv and external diff drivers, fsmonitor and hooks are switched off for every git call.

entries.name: john
entries.title: John the Ripper
entries.description: Password hash cracking with John the Ripper (bleeding-jumbo, CPU only): wordlist mode with rules (the bundled password.lst or your wordlist from /work), single crack and incremental mode, for a bounded time, with autodetected or chosen hash format; extract_hash turns protected zip, rar, PDF, Office, SSH key and KeePass files from /work into crackable hashes. No network.
entries.license: MIT (MCP server, axross-mcp-hub) AND GPL-2.0-or-later with relaxed terms for components (John the Ripper jumbo; unRAR code under its own licence)

mounts.description: Optional: wordlists and protected files (read-only is enough)

entries.notes: Crack only hashes you are authorized to crack. Hashes go to a private temporary file, never onto a command line; each run ends after max_seconds (at most 30 minutes), and the pot file is discarded with the run.

entries.name: mcpcap
entries.title: mcpcap (PCAP analysis)
entries.description: Analyzes packet captures (.pcap, .pcapng, .cap) with scapy: DNS, DHCP, ICMP, SIP, TCP connections, anomalies, retransmissions, traffic flows and capinfos-style statistics. Files are read from the folder mounted at /work (tools take /work/<file>). No network.

mounts.description: The folder with the capture files (read-only is enough)

entries.notes: mcpcap can also download a capture from an http(s) URL; with no network (the default) that fails, which is intended.

entries.name: nmap
entries.title: Nmap
entries.description: Network reconnaissance with Nmap: TCP connect port scans, service and version detection, NSE scripts and a quick top-100 scan, with parsed results. Needs network: Full (scans go to arbitrary hosts and ports, which an HTTP allowlist cannot carry).
entries.license: MIT (MCP server, FuzzingLabs) AND Nmap licence (GPL-2.0 with clarifications, Debian package)
entries.notes: TCP connect scans only: axross grants the container no NET_RAW, so SYN, UDP and OS-detection scans are not offered. Scan only systems you are authorized to test.

entries.name: nuclei
entries.title: Nuclei (ProjectDiscovery)
entries.description: Template-based vulnerability scanning with ProjectDiscovery nuclei and a pinned nuclei-templates release: full scans with severity and tag filters, a quick high/critical scan, and scans by category (cves, exposures, misconfiguration, technologies, default-logins, takeovers, network, ssl, dns, ...). Needs network: Full.
entries.notes: Interactsh (out-of-band callbacks through a third-party server) and template updates are off. A scan with every template can exceed axross's 512 MiB memory limit: prefer categories, tags or severities. Scan only systems you are authorized to test.

entries.name: radare2
entries.title: radare2 (r2mcp)
entries.description: Reverse engineering with radare2 through its official MCP server r2mcp: open a binary, analyze, list functions, imports, strings and sections, disassemble, decompile (r2's pdc), cross references. Binaries are read from the folder mounted at /work (open_file takes /work/<file>); r2mcp refuses paths outside /work. No network.
entries.license: MIT (r2mcp) AND LGPL-3.0-only (radare2; some plugins GPL-3.0, Apache-2.0, BSD)

mounts.description: The folder with the binaries to analyze (read-only is enough)

entries.notes: radare2's own sandbox is on (no shell, no sockets, no file writes) and the raw run_command / run_javascript tools are off. The sql tool needs the r2xsql plugin, which is not included.

entries.name: sleuthkit
entries.title: The Sleuth Kit
entries.description: Disk image forensics with The Sleuth Kit 4.12: partition tables (mmls), file system details (fsstat), file listings including deleted entries (fls), inode metadata (istat), reading a file's content by inode (icat, also deleted files), extracting it to /out, and a MAC timeline (fls + mactime). Images (raw/dd, E01 where supported) are read from the folder mounted at /work. No network.
entries.license: MIT (MCP server, axross-mcp-hub) AND CPL-1.0, IPL-1.0 and others (The Sleuth Kit, Debian package; see its copyright file)

mounts.description: The folder with the disk images (read-only is enough)
A folder for extracted files (tick writable)

entries.notes: read_file returns at most 1 MiB of a file (text or hex); extract_file writes the whole file into /out and never overwrites. The image is only read.

entries.name: sqlmap
entries.title: sqlmap
entries.description: SQL injection detection and exploitation with sqlmap: scan a URL, test a parameter, enumerate databases, tables and columns, dump table data. Needs network: Full.
entries.license: MIT (MCP server, FuzzingLabs) AND GPL-2.0-or-later (sqlmap, with its clarifications)
entries.notes: sqlmap changes data on the target only through what you ask for (dump reads). Test only systems you are authorized to test.

entries.name: tshark
entries.title: TShark (Wireshark)
entries.description: Packet capture analysis with Wireshark's TShark 4.4: capture summary (capinfos), protocol hierarchy, conversations, endpoints, packets with display filters and chosen fields, TCP/UDP/HTTP stream contents, HTTP requests, DNS queries and clear-text credentials. Captures (.pcap, .pcapng) are read from the folder mounted at /work. No network: TShark only reads files, never captures and never resolves names.
entries.license: MIT (MCP server, axross-mcp-hub) AND GPL-2.0-or-later (Wireshark/TShark, Debian package)

mounts.description: The folder with the capture files (read-only is enough)

entries.notes: Display filters and field names are validated and passed as single arguments; a capture is parsed by Wireshark's dissectors inside the container (no capabilities, no network).

entries.name: yara
entries.title: YARA
entries.description: Scans files and folders with YARA: the bundled Yara-Rules subset (crypto constants, packers, anti-debug/anti-VM, capabilities), your own rule files, or inline rules. Targets are read from the folder mounted at /work; extra rule files can be mounted at /rules. No network.
entries.license: MIT (MCP server, FuzzingLabs) AND BSD-3-Clause (YARA) AND GPL-2.0-only (bundled Yara-Rules)

mounts.description: The folder to scan (read-only is enough)
A folder with your own .yar rule files

entries.notes: Inline rules may not use include. Directory scans do not follow symbolic links.
